lessons.title: Traditional Coding vs. AI
lessons.content_md:
# Traditional Coding vs. AI 🤖

For the last 50 years, programming has worked exactly the same way: Humans write the **rules**, give the computer some **data**, and the computer gives back the **answers**.

Imagine you want a computer to identify pictures of apples.

In traditional coding, a programmer has to write a massive list of rules:
1. IF the shape is perfectly round...
2. AND the color is red or green...
3. AND there is a small brown stick on top...
4. THEN it is an apple.

But what if the apple is half-eaten? What if the photo is blurry? Traditional code breaks instantly because humans can't possibly write a rule for every single scenario.

<flipcard front="📜 How does traditional programming work?" back="Humans write a rigid set of rules (the code). The computer blindly follows those rules to process data and produce an answer."></flipcard>

## Flipping the Script

Artificial Intelligence (specifically Machine Learning) flips this entire process upside down.

Instead of giving the computer the rules, we give the computer the **data** (10,000 pictures of apples) and the **answers** (we label them "This is an apple").

The computer then uses math to figure out the **rules** on its own!

It analyzes the 10,000 pictures, notices patterns we wouldn't even think of, and builds its own internal logic for what an apple looks like.

<flipcard front="🧠 How is Machine Learning different?" back="Instead of writing rules, we feed the computer Data and Answers. The computer then learns the Patterns and writes the Rules itself!"></flipcard>
